From bc7304f3ae20972d11db6e0b1b541c63feda5f05 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sebastian Andrzej Siewior <bigeasy@linutronix.de>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 12:34:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] futex: Prevent lockup in requeue-PI during signal/ timeout
 wakeup

During wait-requeue-pi (task A) and requeue-PI (task B) the following
race can happen:

     Task A                             Task B
  futex_wait_requeue_pi()
    futex_setup_timer()
    futex_do_wait()
                                   futex_requeue()
                                        CLASS(hb, hb1)(&key1);
                                        CLASS(hb, hb2)(&key2);
        *timeout*
    futex_requeue_pi_wakeup_sync()
        requeue_state = Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE

    *blocks on hb->lock*

                                        futex_proxy_trylock_atomic()
                                          futex_requeue_pi_prepare()
                                            Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE => -EAGAIN
                                        double_unlock_hb(hb1, hb2)
                                         *retry*

Task B acquires both hb locks and attempts to acquire the PI-lock of the
top most waiter (task B). Task A is leaving early due to a signal/
timeout and started removing itself from the queue. It updates its
requeue_state but can not remove it from the list because this requires
the hb lock which is owned by task B.

Usually task A is able to swoop the lock after task B unlocked it.
However if task B is of higher priority then task A may not be able to
wake up in time and acquire the lock before task B gets it again.
Especially on a UP system where A is never scheduled.

As a result task A blocks on the lock and task B busy loops, trying to
make progress but live locks the system instead. Tragic.

This can be fixed by removing the top most waiter from the list in this
case. This allows task B to grab the next top waiter (if any) in the
next iteration and make progress.

Remove the top most waiter if futex_requeue_pi_prepare() fails.
Let the waiter conditionally remove itself from the list in
handle_early_requeue_pi_wakeup().

Fixes: 07d91ef510fb1 ("futex: Prevent requeue_pi() lock nesting issue on RT")
Reported-by: Moritz Klammler <Moritz.Klammler@ferchau.com>
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Andrzej Siewior <bigeasy@linutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260428103425.dywXyPd3@linutronix.de
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/VE1PR06MB6894BE61C173D802365BE19DFF4CA@VE1PR06MB6894.eurprd06.prod.outlook.com

diff --git a/kernel/futex/requeue.c b/kernel/futex/requeue.c
index d818b4d47f1b..b597cb3d17fc 100644
--- a/kernel/futex/requeue.c
+++ b/kernel/futex/requeue.c
@@ -319,8 +319,11 @@ futex_proxy_trylock_atomic(u32 __user *pifutex, struct futex_hash_bucket *hb1,
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* Ensure that this does not race against an early wakeup */
-	if (!futex_requeue_pi_prepare(top_waiter, NULL))
+	if (!futex_requeue_pi_prepare(top_waiter, NULL)) {
+		plist_del(&top_waiter->list, &hb1->chain);
+		futex_hb_waiters_dec(hb1);
 		return -EAGAIN;
+	}
 
 	/*
 	 * Try to take the lock for top_waiter and set the FUTEX_WAITERS bit
@@ -722,10 +725,12 @@ int handle_early_requeue_pi_wakeup(struct futex_hash_bucket *hb,
 
 	/*
 	 * We were woken prior to requeue by a timeout or a signal.
-	 * Unqueue the futex_q and determine which it was.
+	 * Conditionally unqueue the futex_q and determine which it was.
 	 */
-	plist_del(&q->list, &hb->chain);
-	futex_hb_waiters_dec(hb);
+	if (!plist_node_empty(&q->list)) {
+		plist_del(&q->list, &hb->chain);
+		futex_hb_waiters_dec(hb);
+	}
 
 	/* Handle spurious wakeups gracefully */
 	ret = -EWOULDBLOCK;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

This patch fixes a livelock scenario in the futex requeue-PI mechanism, where a high-priority task performing a requeue (Task B) can busy-loop indefinitely because the leaving waiter (Task A) cannot remove itself from the waiter list while Task B holds the hash bucket locks. The fix introduces two coordinated changes in `kernel/futex/requeue.c`:

### 1. `futex_proxy_trylock_atomic()` – proactive removal of the top waiter

When `futex_requeue_pi_prepare()` fails (indicating the top waiter is leaving due to signal/timeout), the requeuer now immediately removes that waiter from the hash bucket’s plist and decrements the waiters count before returning `-EAGAIN`. Previously it only returned `-EAGAIN` without altering the list, which caused the requeuer to keep retrying on the same unavailable waiter.

### 2. `handle_early_requeue_pi_wakeup()` – conditional self-removal

The waiter’s early-wakeup handler now checks whether its plist node is still on the list before attempting to remove itself. This is necessary because the requeuer (via the first change) may have already removed the waiter from the list. Attempting a double removal would corrupt the list and lead to undefined behavior.

### Relationship Between the Changes

The two modifications are complementary and interdependent:

- The first change ensures that when a requeue attempt cannot proceed with the current top waiter (because it is leaving), the requeuer takes the responsibility of removing that waiter from the list. This unblocks the requeue loop, allowing it to pick the next waiter and make progress.

- The second change ensures that the leaving waiter does not redundantly try to remove itself after the requeuer has already done so. Without this check, the waiter would attempt to delete a node that is no longer in the list, causing list corruption or a hang.

Together, these changes break the deadlock cycle: Task B (requeue) no longer spins on an unresponsive waiter, and Task A (leaving waiter) safely skips self-removal when it has been removed already. The fix resolves the livelock, especially on UP systems where task priority prevents the leaving waiter from acquiring the lock in time.
